# Requirements Quality Checklist: Homepage Useful Information Hub

**Purpose**: Validate that homepage information hub requirements are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before implementation finalization.
**Created**: 2026-10-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements explicitly documented for every mandatory homepage element (search, toolkit, clocks, four GitHub widgets, and calendar widget)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001..FR-013]
- [ ] CHK002 Are all toolkit link requirements complete, including labels and fixed destination URLs for each required tool? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002..FR-006]
- [ ] CHK003 Are separate requirement statements present for each GitHub work category (opened issues, assigned issues, opened PRs, review-requested PRs)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009..FR-012]
- [ ] CHK004 Are calendar requirements complete for scope boundaries of "today" and "primary calendar" behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is "at the top of the homepage" defined with unambiguous placement criteria (for example, above all widgets in default viewport)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK006 Are "open" GitHub issue and pull request criteria clearly defined (status semantics and inclusion boundaries)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009..FR-012]
- [ ] CHK007 Is local time display behavior clearly specified (timezone label format, refresh behavior, and source of local timezone)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Do user-scoped data requirements align across GitHub and Google sources so both consistently use each signed-in user's linked authorization? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK009 Are degraded-state requirements consistent between no-data scenarios and unavailable-service scenarios across all personalized widgets? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014; Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK010 Do layout-variant requirements remain consistent with "layout not yet finalized" while still requiring all widgets/links in every variant? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015..FR-016; Spec §Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK011 Do success criteria cover all required widget groups, not only search/toolkit/clocks, so acceptance is complete for full feature scope? [Gap, Spec §SC-001; Spec §FR-009..FR-013]
- [ ] CHK012 Are link-destination success criteria objectively measurable for all required toolkit links? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002; Spec §FR-003..FR-006]
- [ ] CHK013 Are timing/usability targets defined with clear measurement conditions (sample size, user cohort, and measurement method)? [Clarity, Spec §SC-003..SC-004]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "distinct layout screenshot/mockup" acceptance defined with objective distinctness criteria for stakeholder comparison? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-005; Spec §FR-015]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements explicitly documented for primary, alternate, and exception flows for each external integration (GitHub and Google Calendar)? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories; Spec §FR-008..FR-014]
- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements defined for authorization-loss scenarios (for example, previously linked account access revoked) and expected homepage behavior? [Gap, Exception Flow]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for data refresh expectations (initial load only vs periodic refresh/manual refresh) for personalized widgets? [Gap]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK018 Are empty-state requirements complete for each personalized widget when a user has no issues, PRs, review requests, or events? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases; Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK019 Is fallback behavior specified when local timezone cannot be resolved, including what timezone label/value is shown? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases; Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK020 Are partial-outage requirements defined so unaffected widgets remain usable while one external dependency fails? [Coverage, Spec §FR-014; Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK021 Are performance requirements specified for personalized widget loading and timeout thresholds? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [ ] CHK022 Are accessibility requirements defined for keyboard navigation, screen reader semantics, and focus order across homepage widgets? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [ ] CHK023 Are privacy and data-visibility requirements defined to ensure only the signed-in user's personal GitHub/Calendar data is displayed? [Gap, Non-Functional]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK024 Are external dependency constraints (API limits, pagination expectations, and downtime behavior) documented as explicit requirements or assumptions? [Dependency, Gap]
- [ ] CHK025 Are assumptions about linked accounts and prior authorization converted into explicit behavior requirements when assumptions are not met? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions; Spec §FR-014]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK026 Is conflict resolution defined for cases where stakeholder-selected layout preferences could reduce required widget visibility or hierarchy? [Conflict, Spec §FR-015..FR-016]
- [ ] CHK027 Are all materially testable requirements traceable to stable IDs (including missing non-functional requirements) to prevent acceptance gaps? [Traceability, Gap]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
